title: Microdrop Battleblitz: 5-slide ops playbook (draft)
summary: Working sketch for a hyper-compact sales enablement micro-deck aimed at platform/ops stakeholders. Emphasis: rapid pilot decision (5 slides), technical risk mitigations, and canned fallback scripts for sellers. This is a tactical deliverable to pair with existing longer playbooks — goal is a 2-minute seller walkthrough + 1-page handoff for eng leads.
audience: Primary: SEs and AEs doing quick pilot qualification with platform engineers and SRE/infra leads. Secondary: Field sellers prepping for 15-30 min technical discovery calls.
core_messages: Redwood gives predictable inference economics: choose hosted for speed, dedicated for capacity predictability, private for compliance; same API everywhere.
Operational controls (batching, cache, quant profiles) let you trade 2-5x cost for 10-50% latency improvements depending on workload.
Graceful fallbacks keep apps responsive: routing policies + automatic model variant downgrade instead of hard failures.
Pilot fast: two-week technical validation path with clear success metrics (p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rate).
slide_outline: Slide 1 — One-sentence value & ask: what we want from the call (pilot scope + success metrics). Example: 'Validate 4k daily inference volume for 2 weeks; target p95 < 300ms; cost < $0.002/token equivalent.'
Slide 2 — Quick architecture sketch: sample integration patterns (direct API, SDK + edge caching, dedicated pool). Callouts: data plane isolation, KMS options, no model retraining needed.

Slide 3 — Risk & fallback playbook: common failure modes (burst throttling, KV cache cold starts, token-embedding mismatch) and immediate mitigations (auto-route, smaller model fallback, prefix cache priming).
Slide 4 — Pilot runbook & measurable gates: telemetry to watch (latency percentiles, tail queue length, token cost per request), canary traffic split, rollback triggers.
Slide 5 — Seller script & handoff checklist: 2-min scripts for common objections + engineering checklist for handoff to SRE/infra.
battlecard_snippets: Customer: 'We can't sacrifice latency for cost.' Response: 'We configure latency SLOs first; Optimize gives batching and cache knobs that reduce cost while keeping p95 within your SLO.'
Customer: 'We have compliance concerns.' Response: 'Private deployments and VPC-private control plane options with KMS support; we can scope a short on-prem proof for audits.'
Customer: 'What happens if we hit capacity?' Response: 'Smart routing + reserved pools for critical routes and automatic model variant fallback to preserve availability.'
objection_handlers: Objection: Model quality drift vs quantized models. Handler: share eval snapshot + prompt set we used; recommend A/B compare using Redwood Optimize and threshold-based rollouts.
Objection: 'We host everything internally.' Handler: emphasize consistent API and private deployment option; propose a short security review + architecture workshop.
Objection: Pricing unpredictability. Handler: propose a short reserved capacity estimate and show how batching/prefix caching reduces per-token unit costs.
quick_checklist: Pre-call: attach pilot one-pager + example telemetry dashboard template (create ticket CONFLUENCE:CONF-2312).
During call: confirm spike volume, token distribution, and red team/PII needs.
Post-call: create GTMPILOT JIRA ticket with target SLOs, assign eng lead, schedule 30-min kickoff with infra (SLA & routing policy decisions).
Engineer handoff checklist: API key scope, VPC connectivity notes (if private), preferred model family and fallback threshold, telemetry endpoints.
Seller script snap: two opening lines, one technical qualifier, one closing ask (pilot sign-off).
open_questions: Do we want a single canonical dashboard JSON for pilot telemetry or allow teams to copy a template? (ops preference).
Which internal legal checklist items must be pre-cleared for a private pilot (data residency vs on-prem)?
How aggressive should default quantization recommendations be for trial workloads (Q4_8 vs Q5_6)? Need APPLIED-ML input.
